before: Issue #533 -- one line a site manager keeps on this asset: what sets it apart from the others of its kind, or where it is kept. At most 50 characters, trimmed with runs of spaces collapsed and case kept, and blank where it has none -- the app writes null to clear it. Written, changed and cleared on the asset's page by a site manager on the asset's Job (#597) while the asset is In stock or Out (lib/assetStatus.js:MAY_WRITE_NOTE_IN_STATUS); read by everyone else, and while it is In repair or Retired. NOT AN EVENT: changing it appends no Asset Log row and moves neither Status nor Job, so nothing records who wrote it or when, and a category's list does not count it as a change. Not printed on the label. lib/assetNote.js holds the rule. A serial number has a field of its own since #601, Serial Number.

before: Issue #601 -- the serial number this asset's maker gave it, one line. Kept trimmed with runs of spaces collapsed and its case as typed, and blank where it has none -- the app writes null to clear it. At most 50 characters, app-enforced. Two assets of one Category cannot hold one serial number, compared without regard to case or surrounding spaces; a Deleted asset does not count and a Retired one does. The app reads the base again as it saves and refuses, naming the asset that holds it (lib/assetSerial.js). Written, changed and cleared on the asset's page by a site manager on the asset's Job while it is In stock or Out, as Note is (lib/assetStatus.js:MAY_WRITE_NOTE_IN_STATUS); read by everyone else. NOT AN EVENT: changing it appends no Asset Log row and moves neither Status nor Job. The Equipment & Tools list's search finds an asset by it at any job, and its export carries it. Made by scripts/import/add_serial_number_601.mjs on both bases.
